configuration: Official test12, RNX2RTKP -p 0 with unchanged positioning defaults, all 120 GPS observation epochs on 2005-04-02 GPST 00:00:00..00:59:30; dms output.
observable: Per-epoch position, solution validity, satellite count, physical time and six printed signed square-root covariance entries (sdn,sde,sdu,sdne,sdeu,sdun)
runtime_note: Conservative run-only budget of 0.25 s; observed ARM64 container check-driver time excluding measured compilation was approximately 0.05–0.06 s in calibration 20260917T042746Z. Includes Python/file overhead; not a solver-kernel benchmark.
default_vs_upstream: upstream: same numerical flags and input bytes; only input/output paths relocated; redundant -r retained and unused by SPP
variant: First epoch G11 C1 pseudorange 20311445.258 -> 20311445.260 m (+0.002 m, two last printed units). All other observation bytes and the navigation file are unchanged. This is rounding-noise calibration, not a new physical scenario.
altbuild: Clang -O3 instead of GCC -O3 with otherwise identical source/flags and nominal inputs; both are legitimate IEEE-oriented builds with no fast-math, and both compilers are installed in the image.

comparison.rule: Match records by physical input epoch, require identical accepted/rejected masks, SPP status and used-satellite counts; compare each WGS84 ECEF position component within 0.05 m, six printed signed square-root covariance entries (sdn,sde,sdu,sdne,sdeu,sdun) within 0.05 m, and physical timestamps within 0.001 s; the largest field error divided by its bound must be <= 1.0. Exclude header paths, row order, age/ambiguity ratio and NMEA hard-coded HDOP or unavailable Doppler speed/course.

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck on 2026-09-17: run.sh altbuild (Clang -O3 instead of GCC -O3, same source, flags, library and nominal inputs; no fast-math.) against run.sh nominal, graded with the check's own validate.py: every graded value identical, an ungraded file differs

tolerance_status: Numerical policy finalised by contributor Weixuan Liao at 2026-09-17T04:52:00+00:00: “认可这些规则，继续本机复验”. Cross-architecture adequacy remains unresolved; SCC run is paused, and no curator scientific acceptance is claimed.
warrant: This is numerical preservation of the official GPS SPP workload, not a claim of centimetre-level true positioning accuracy. src/pntpos.c:346 stops least squares at a 1e-4 update norm, and src/solution.c:988-999 prints millimetre-or-finer coordinates and float-stored covariance terms; NMEA heights print to 0.001 m at solution.c:1087. The proposed 0.05 m field bounds are above these representation scales and the injected 0.002 m input change, while metre-scale coordinate faults should fail; calibration 20260917T042746Z measured 1.572–1.713 mm position-component movement and at most 2 mm auxiliary movement, with at least 25x bound headroom. Native metre-scale fault probes were rejected. These facts defend the selected scale for this dataset, not universal portability. The 0.001 s timestamp bound allows the relevant display rounding (10 ns for the nine-decimal format). The 13 s GPST-minus-UTC value follows the pinned leap-second table for April 2005, not the host clock. Exact epoch-mask checks reject silently dropped or spurious fixes. The nominal fixture's late poor geometry is retained. At 2026-09-17T04:52:00+00:00, the contributor reviewed the disclosed evidence and limitations and accepted these numerical rules (“认可这些规则，继续本机复验”). GCC/Clang graded values were identical in all seven checks, so a zero recorded floor remains uninformative; cross-architecture evidence or a curator ruling is still needed. The contributor has not authorised the prepared SCC run.
